summary: If a man warned his wife and then heard she was alone with that man, Rabbi Eliezer says he must divorce her even if he heard it from a bird. Rabbi Yehoshua says only once everyone is talking about it.

chunks.en: If a man warned his wife and she was alone (with that man),
chunks.st: one who warned his wife not to seclude herself with a particular man and she subsequently secluded herself with the man she was warned about,

chunks.en: even if he heard it from a flying bird,
chunks.st: even if he heard about it from a flying bird, or any other source whatsoever,

chunks.en: he must divorce her and give her the kesubah.
chunks.st: he must divorce his wife. However, he must still grant her the money accorded to her by her marriage contract
chunks.stMore: because there is no actual proof of her seclusion with the man in question.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer,
chunks.stMore: who, as quoted in the first mishna of the tractate (2a), holds that there is no necessity for witnesses to testify with regard to the seclusion, and the woman becomes forbidden to her husband even in the absence of witnesses, by the husband’s word alone.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua disagrees, as he did in the mishna (2a), and says:

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיִּשְׂאוּ וְיִתְּנוּ בָהּ מוֹזְרוֹת בַּלְּבָנָה:
chunks.en: Not until the women who spin thread by moonlight talk about her.
chunks.st: He does not divorce his wife in the absence of witnesses until the gossiping women who sit and spin thread by the light of the moon begin to discuss her
chunks.stMore: behavior, as they share the gossip of the town. The Gemara earlier (6b) taught that a woman whose infidelity became subject to this public discussion can no longer be tested by the bitter water of a sota. Consequently, she must get divorced.

summary: Even one witness, or even a servant, is believed that the woman sinned, so she does not drink. Some women relatives are believed only so that she does not drink, but she still gets her kesubah.
stIntro: The mishna continues to list various possible testimonies concerning of such acts of seclusion. If

chunks.en: If one witness said,
chunks.st: one witness said:

chunks.en: "I saw that she became tamei,"
chunks.st: I saw that she became defiled
chunks.stMore: during her seclusion by engaging in sexual intercourse with that other man,

chunks.en: she does not drink.
chunks.st: she does not drink
chunks.stMore: the bitter water, but rather, he divorces her immediately.

chunks.en: And more than that: even a servant,
chunks.st: And furthermore, even if the one who testified was a slave

chunks.en: even a maidservant,
chunks.st: or a maidservant,
chunks.stMore: neither of whom is generally regarded as a valid witness,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ נֶאֱמָנִין אַף לְפָסְלָהּ מִכְּתֻבָּתָהּ.
chunks.en: is believed, even to make her lose her kesubah.
chunks.st: they are deemed credible to testify to the wife’s adultery even to the extent that their testimony disqualifies her from receiving her marriage contract
chunks.stMore: and prevents her from drinking the bitter water. The mishna continues by listing women whose testimony is only partially accepted concerning this matter:

chunks.en: Her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, her husband's other wife,
chunks.st: Her mother-in-law, and her mother in-law’s daughter, and her rival wife, i.e., a second wife of the husband,

words.note: Another wife of the same husband.

chunks.en: her husband's brother's wife, and her husband's daughter —
chunks.st: and her yevama, i.e., her husband’s brother’s wife, and her husband’s daughter,
chunks.stMore: all of whom are generally not deemed credible if they say anything incriminating pertaining to this woman due to the tumultuous relationships these women often have.

chunks.en: they are believed,
chunks.st: They are all deemed credible
chunks.stMore: to testify concerning the woman’s defilement while in seclusion,

chunks.en: but not to make her lose her kesubah,
chunks.st: but are not deemed credible to the extent that their testimony will disqualify her from receiving her marriage contract;

chunks.en: only so that she will not drink.
chunks.st: rather, it is deemed credible to the extent that she will not drink of the bitter water of a sota.

summary: Why is one witness enough to say she became tamei, but two are needed to say she was alone with the man? The mishna shows that logic alone would say the opposite, so we learn it from pesukim.
stIntro: This ruling allowing one witness’s testimony with regard to defilement needs to be stated,

chunks.en: For by logic it should be:
chunks.st: as, by right, it should not have been
chunks.stMore: deemed credible based on the following a fortiori inference:

chunks.en: if the first testimony (that she was alone with him),
chunks.st: And just as if with regard to the first testimony concerning seclusion,

chunks.en: which does not forbid her forever,
chunks.st: which does not forbid her with an irrevocable prohibition,
chunks.stMore: as the woman can be found innocent permitting her again to her husband by drinking the bitter water,

chunks.en: needs at least two witnesses,
chunks.st: is not established with fewer than two
chunks.stMore: witnesses, since according to the mishna the testimony of seclusion requires two witnesses, then with regard to

chunks.en: then the last testimony (that she became tamei), which forbids her forever,
chunks.st: the final testimony concerning defilement, which forbids her to her husband with an irrevocable prohibition,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא תִתְקַיֵּם בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁנָיִם,
chunks.en: surely should also need at least two witnesses!
chunks.st: is it not logical that it should also not be established with fewer than two witnesses?

chunks.en: So the pasuk says, "And there is no witness against her" —
chunks.st: Therefore, to counter this derivation, the verse states: “And there be no witness against her” (Numbers 5:13),

chunks.en: any testimony against her is enough.
chunks.st: teaching that any testimony with regard to defilement that there is against her
chunks.stMore: is sufficient, and two witnesses are not required.

chunks.en: Now we can learn a kal vachomer for the first testimony:
chunks.st: The Gemara asks: And from now that it is established that one witness suffices to testify with regard to defilement, an a fortiori inference can be made with regard to the first testimony of seclusion:

words.note: Kal vachomer: learning a bigger thing from a smaller thing.

chunks.en: If the last testimony,
chunks.st: And just as if concerning the final testimony of defilement,

chunks.en: which forbids her forever,
chunks.st: which forbids her with an irrevocable prohibition,

chunks.en: is accepted with one witness,
chunks.st: yet it is established by one witness,

chunks.he: עֵדוּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁאֵין אוֹסַרְתָּהּ אִסּוּר עוֹלָם,
chunks.en: then the first testimony, which does not forbid her forever,
chunks.st: then with regard to the first testimony, which does not forbid her with an irrevocable prohibition,

chunks.en: surely should be accepted with one witness!
chunks.st: is it not logical that it should be established with only one witness?

chunks.en: So the pasuk says,
chunks.st: Therefore, to counter this derivation, the verse states:
chunks.stMore: “When a man takes a wife, and marries her, and it comes to pass, if she finds no favor in his eyes,

chunks.en: "because he found in her something wrong (a davar),"
chunks.st: because he has found some unseemly matter [davar] in her” (Deuteronomy 24:1),

chunks.en: and in another place it says,
chunks.st: and there, in the laws concerning monetary matters, it states: “

chunks.he: עַל פִּי שְׁנֵי עֵדִים יָקוּם דָּבָר,
chunks.en: "By the word of two witnesses a davar (matter) shall stand."
chunks.st: At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall a matter [davar] be established” (Deuteronomy 19:15),

chunks.he: מַה לְּהַלָּן עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים,
chunks.en: Just as there it is by two witnesses,
chunks.st: teaching that just as the “matter” stated there is established “at the mouth of two witnesses,”

chunks.he: אַף כָּאן עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים:
chunks.en: so here too it is by two witnesses.
chunks.st: so too, here the “matter” of her seclusion must be established “at the mouth of two witnesses.”

summary: What happens when witnesses argue about whether she became tamei: if it is one against one, or one against two, she drinks. If two say she became tamei, she does not drink.
stIntro: The mishna discusses the halakha in a case where two single witnesses contradict each other concerning her defilement. If one

chunks.he: עֵד אוֹמֵר נִטְמֵאת וְעֵד אוֹמֵר לֹא נִטְמֵאת,
chunks.en: If one witness says she became tamei and one witness says she did not,
chunks.st: witness says: She was defiled, and another witness says: She was not defiled,
chunks.stMore: or similarly in the case of those normally disqualified from bearing witness, if one

chunks.he: אִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת נִטְמֵאת וְאִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת לֹא נִטְמֵאת,
chunks.en: or one woman says she became tamei and one woman says she did not,
chunks.st: woman says: She was defiled, and another woman says: She was not defiled,

chunks.en: she drinks.
chunks.st: she would drink
chunks.stMore: the bitter water of a sota, due to the uncertainty engendered by the contradictory testimonies.

chunks.he: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר נִטְמֵאת וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים לֹא נִטְמֵאת,
chunks.en: If one says she became tamei and two say she did not,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one witness says: She was defiled, and two witnesses say: She was not defiled,

chunks.en: she drinks.
chunks.st: she would drink the bitter water.

chunks.he: שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים נִטְמֵאת וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר לֹא נִטְמֵאת,
chunks.en: If two say she became tamei and one says she did not,
chunks.st: However, if two would say: She was defiled, and one says: She was not defiled,
chunks.stMore: the testimony of the two witnesses is accepted and

chunks.en: she does not drink.
chunks.st: she would not drink
chunks.stMore: the bitter water, and the husband must divorce her.
